question: Asymptomatic bacteriuria in pregnancy is diagnosed when a mid-stream urine culture grows how many colony-forming units (CFU) per mL of a single organism?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: 10³ CFU/mL is below the standard threshold for ASB diagnosis; this level may reflect contamination.
Correct. ASB in pregnancy is defined as ≥10⁵ CFU/mL of a single organism on a single mid-stream urine culture in an asymptomatic woman. Treatment is mandatory in pregnancy.
10⁴ CFU/mL is an intermediate count; the standard diagnostic threshold for ASB is ≥10⁵ CFU/mL.

answers.text: Any growth of E. coli regardless of colony count

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Colony count matters; contamination and true infection must be distinguished. A threshold of ≥10⁵ CFU/mL is required.

overallFeedback.feedback: The diagnostic threshold for asymptomatic bacteriuria is ≥10⁵ CFU/mL of a single organism. This threshold applies to the mandatory screening at first antenatal visit.
Correct. ≥10⁵ CFU/mL single organism on MSU = ASB. Unlike non-pregnant adults, ASB in pregnancy must always be treated.
